name: Private rental repairs deadline tracker
demand: There is a substantial need base in England: 4.7 million private-rented households in 2024/25 and around 2.3 million landlords, according to a House of Commons committee report (https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5902/cmselect/cmcomloc/42/report.html). The 2024 English Private Landlord Survey found that 26% of direct landlords had identified damp or mould in at least one property and 18% had received a tenant complaint in the prior year; its findings do not fully represent agent-managed tenancies (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report). The 2024/25 English Housing Survey estimated surveyor-assessed damp in 11% of private-renter homes (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-housing-survey-2024-to-2025-perceptions-and-impacts-of-housing-quality/english-housing-survey-2024-to-2025-perceptions-and-impacts-of-housing-quality). These establish a problem, not demand for this product. Category search volumes and total installs or active users are unverified; Google Play shows 5+ downloads for the adjacent Lendmark app, but that listing is not a category estimate (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.lendmark.app).
prices: Current rendered Letavo pricing says free for up to 3 properties and £9/month for unlimited; a cached page version surfaced during research showed different tiers, so confirm at checkout (https://letavo.co.uk/pricing/). Lettie advertises free for up to 4 properties, then £2.50 per property/month (https://asklettie.com/). Lettable advertises £19, £49 and £99 monthly tiers (https://www.lettable.co/pricing). Fixflo lists a £75/month software fee plus quoted pricing, and a contractor marketplace from £0.30/unit/month; its listed pricing applies to customers with at least 50 properties (https://www.fixflo.com/pricing/lettings). These are advertised prices, not proof of sales.
copy_speed: Fast. Harthing’s founder says it launched on 12 May 2026 (https://harthing.co.uk/the-record); Letavo’s builder case study labels its launch as May 2026 (https://hailes.tech/work/letavo); and a Lettie press release dated 4 August 2026 announces a free maintenance-reporting plan (https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/24270). LetSync advertises a free repair-tracking service scheduled to open on 15 December 2026, so it is not yet a launched competitor as of 23 October (https://www.letsync.co/). These launch and plan dates are provider or press-release claims, not adoption evidence.
platform_risk: A browser and email-based tracker could avoid dependence on a single platform. Bundling risk is high: existing products already combine repair reporting, audit records and compliance features, including Fixflo (https://www.fixflo.com/pricing/lettings) and Lettie (https://asklettie.com/). If the product depends on WhatsApp or CRM integration to compete, it takes on partner risk; Lettie advertises WhatsApp triage and a two-way Apex27 integration (https://theintermediary.co.uk/2026/09/lettie-integrates-with-apex27-to-streamline-maintenance-for-letting-agents/).
defensible_asset: Weak at launch. The private-rental rules and exact deadlines are still being consulted on, so a rules engine would need frequent updates and would not be a settled, exclusive dataset (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences). A trusted case history, evidence trail and CRM integrations could create switching friction, but competitors already advertise similar audit reports and repair histories (https://asklettie.com/, https://www.fixflo.com/pricing/lettings). A proprietary anonymised repair-outcomes dataset is only a possible future asset; its existence and defensibility are unverified.
build_effort: Moderate for a narrow web product: tenant intake, configurable case states and clocks, reminders, permissioned evidence uploads, versioned rules and an exportable audit record. AI agents could handle routine logging, reminders and report drafts, but hazard assessment, emergency escalation and legal-rule changes need human oversight. The government says private-sector regulations must still set the requirements and notes landlords remain ultimately liable even when using agents (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences). The build estimate is an engineering assessment; measured automation and support workload are unverified.
channel: Use inbound search content: a branded, sourced deadline guide or configurable tracker, plus opt-in posts in landlord communities that permit them. Do not cold-message individual landlords. The 2024 survey says 93% of direct landlords operate as individuals or groups of individuals (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report); ICO guidance says unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals, including sole traders, generally needs consent or a valid soft opt-in, and public contact details do not by themselves mean consent (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/how-do-we-comply-with-the-pecr-electronic-mail-marketing-rules/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; there is no public operating evidence supporting the <=5 h/week constraint. Rule review, product support and urgent-case escalations could require owner time.
desk_test: One-day, no-code test: check actual volume bands in Google Ads Keyword Planner for exact-intent phrases such as “landlord repair tracker” and “Awaab’s Law landlord software” (https://ads.google.com/home/tools/keyword-planner/); do not fill in missing volume. Build a branded page with a clickable report-to-clock-to-evidence mockup and a clearly priced pilot offer, then share it once in a landlord forum that permits research posts. Measure opt-ins and paid intent; no cold email, SMS, WhatsApp or DMs.
red_flags: Research-stage survive only; not yet a build decision. The Renters’ Rights Act provides for extension to private rentals, but regulations must set the requirements; the consultation says 2027 is the earliest feasible date, not a confirmed start date (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences/extending-awaabs-law-to-private-rented-tenancies-and-to-licences). The implementation roadmap lists the private-rental Awaab’s Law date as TBC (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/renters-rights-act-2025-implementation-roadmap/implementing-renters-rights-act-2025-our-roadmap-for-reforming-the-private-rented-sector). Direct competitors already advertise free entry tiers, and no dated, verifiable revenue or paid-customer evidence was found; Latch’s page reports a March 2026 “first customer” milestone but does not say whether it was paid or disclose revenue (https://www.uselatch.co.uk/about). The numeric automation field is 0 because no measured share is verified, not because the product was measured at 0% automation. The >=50% automation and <=5 h/week gates remain unproven.
